per_shot.note: Real hab shell: riveted panels, ribs, conduit, plated floor, a ceiling with three lit fixtures casting pools on the wall; stock reads as a plain but credible room, though the lower 40% is dark empty floor.
Wall pools from fixtures read well and portholes glow dusk; floor is grey-cool and the porthole light does not spill onto it, so the bottom half feels cold and dead.
Cork board, fridge and crates have detail; the east door bay shades nicely to dark, but the floor plane again dominates with little warmth landing on it.
Clearly richer: patterned woven rug, leafy fern in pot, radio with a glowing dial, books on a shelf; every item reads as itself and the room feels cared for.
Arc lamp throws a visible warm cone on wall and floor, star chart reads instantly; best warmth in the set, though the rug and lamp pools are small against the huge dark floor.
Kettle, cups and tiled splashback, bunk with pillow and blanket, wall sconce, lit GALLERY placard with a glimpse of a warm wing beyond: reads as a lived-in sanctuary.

top_issues.issue: The foreground floor takes roughly the lower 40% of every frame and is a cool grey, near-black expanse lit only by the suit's headlamp hotspot.
top_issues.why: It reads grim rather than sanctuary, wastes frame space, and the cool tone fights the warm walls; this is a 'dark corner' grown into half the image.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Warm the floor plating toward the wall's amber-brown, let fixture and lamp pools reach further onto the floor, and add a low warm fill or a lower camera/tighter framing so the floor band is smaller.

top_issues.issue: Dusk from the portholes stays inside the glass; no orange shaft or pool lands on the floor below them.
top_issues.why: The brief asks for porthole dusk spilling onto the floor; it is the cheapest link to the 02-surface lit-window warmth.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add a soft warm-orange spot or projected ellipse on the floor and a faint rim on the porthole frames from each window.

top_issues.issue: Stock walls are one tan value top to bottom; value variation comes only from the fixture cones.
top_issues.why: The stock room should still feel like a good room on its own; the panels have seams but little tonal variety (insulated vs metal, kickplate vs upper panel).
top_issues.suggested_direction: Vary panel values slightly by row (darker kickplate band, lighter insulated upper panels), and add a little grime/gradient toward the corners in flat vertex colour, not texture.

top_issues.issue: Ceiling cross-beams under strong perspective converge diagonally and pull attention up and outward.
top_issues.why: The ceiling is now real and good, but the diagonal beams feel busy and slightly distorted relative to the calm side-view room.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Keep the fixtures and panels but reduce beam contrast or field of view so the ceiling recedes and the wall band stays the focus.

top_issues.issue: Small props (radio, books, kettle) are lit mostly by ambient; only the radio dial and lamp emit.
top_issues.why: Bought things should look cared for; a touch of local light helps them read at play scale.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Let the radio dial and galley sconce throw a small warm pool on their own surfaces and the wall behind.

protect: Real ceiling with lit fixtures and conduit instead of a black slab
Riveted panel walls, ribs, vents and the red trim band
Fixture light pools landing on the wall
Arc lamp's visible warm cone on wall and floor
Patterned woven rug, leafy fern, radio with glowing dial, book spines, kettle and cups, bunk with pillow and bedding, star chart
Lit GALLERY placard and warm glimpse into the wing
Suit remains the brightest, most legible element

per_shot.note: The flat beige box the brief complains about: untextured wall, black slab ceiling, black void below a thin floor strip.
Single flat wall colour, no seams or fixtures; props are flat-shaded blocks and the station screen has no detail.
Cork board is three coloured squares on brown; crates are plain boxes; nothing reads as lived-in.
Fern and book spines read; rug is a flat red slab with no weave or pattern, radio has no glowing dial.
Star chart reads; arc lamp is a white shade with no light pool on wall or floor.
Bunk is a beige slab with a red block for a pillow, galley is a green box with two cups; more stuff but not richer in mood.

top_issues.issue: Ceiling is a black slab and the area below the floor is black void, framing the room as a thin strip.
top_issues.why: Directly contradicts the brief's 'a real ceiling with fixtures, never a black slab'.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Build a paneled ceiling with ribs and lit fixtures, and a plated floor that fills the lower frame.

top_issues.issue: Walls and floor are single flat colours with no panel seams, ribs, conduit or plating.
top_issues.why: This is the 'flat beige box' the player called basic.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Add panel seams, rivets, ribs, vents, kickplate bands and value variation between surfaces.

top_issues.issue: Light does not land: no fixture pools, the arc lamp casts nothing, portholes do not spill.
top_issues.why: 'Light lands, warmly' is the core of the sanctuary mood; the room is evenly dim.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give every practical a warm spot pool on wall and floor, and let the arc lamp throw a visible cone.

top_issues.issue: Furnishings are flat blocks that do not read as themselves: rug has no pattern, radio no dial glow, bunk no bedding, cork board pins are coloured squares.
top_issues.why: The brief lists each item that must read in close-up and at play scale.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Model chunky low-poly detail per item: woven rug pattern, emissive radio dial, pillow and folded blanket, kettle spout and handle.

top_issues.issue: Furnished room is barely richer than stock in mood.
top_issues.why: Buying things should visibly transform the room.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Tie furnishings to added light and colour so each purchase adds a warm pool.

protect: Every station and furnishing in its fixed slot

why: A delivers the brief's hab shell (paneled walls, real lit ceiling, plated floor), landing light, and furnishings that read as themselves; B is still the flat beige box with a black-slab ceiling. A's main gap is a cold, oversized dark floor band.
